**ABSTRACT**

The Smart Educational Institute (SEI) aims to address some of the issues that Educational Institutes encounter. For the Institute's administration and students, SEI will provide a user-friendly interface. The biggest issue that students have with the current university attendance system is that manual entry takes time and is inefficient since a teacher mistake or a student's lack of attention during that time may mark him or her absent, which could be troublesome for students in the future. Another key point is that there is no longer a proxy system. The second issue is security. Because most educational institutes still use the old traditional card system, creating a similar-looking fake ID is not difficult, and a criminal may get admission to the university using a fake ID card. Instead of the old standard barcode card system, RFID smart cards with facial recognition can solve this problem, If a student forgets his or her id card, facial recognition will aid to identify the student, allowing only registered students to enter the institution. Anyone else will have to go through the necessary procedure to enter as a visitor, avoiding any unwanted threat or suspicion. The goal of this project is to create a Smart Institute Model that includes a cross-platform application as well as an IoT system for implementing facial recognition for managing arrival and departure times, as well as accessing late arrivals and early departures to ensure punctuality, Another feature is introduced in light of the circumstances and hazards of COVID-19, and it includes the detection of face masks to check if the individual is following the SOPs or not, also RFID Smart Cards will be utilised to track attendance for classrooms.

1. #  {#heading}

   1. ## **INTRODUCTION** {#introduction}

      1. ### **Background** {#background}

Among college students, skipping classes is a typical occurrence. It is deemed truancy and is classified as one of the university's discipline issues. According to dictionary of Pearson Education Limited, Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English 2003, truancy means “the act or condition of being absent from compulsory education” or “any intentional unauthorized absence from compulsory education”. Poor attendance may result in ineligibility for graduation, as well as the students' inability to take the final examination. According to research conducted in Malaysia, the absenteeism rate among pupils is quite high and can reach a critical level between 20% and 40%.   
\[1\]. Students who are chronically absent from school face a variety of academic challenges.\[2\]. The most common causes for university students not attending courses include waking up late and not having transportation to get to class because the distance between their dorms and lecture hall is rather long. These justifications are insufficient and cannot be accepted. Institutions have established measures to improve student attendance, such as limiting the number of times they can skip specific lectures before being excluded from sitting the subject's final exams. Attendance is also kept track of by handing out an attendance list and asking students to sign it to confirm that they are present in class. However, taking students' attendance using their signature would not solve the problem, as students nowadays are more likely to forge someone's signature to cover for buddies who miss class. As a result, there is no way to handle the problem of tracking and preventing absence. As a result, a better method or system is necessary to address this problem. To combat fraudulent signatures and resolve attendance difficulties among college or university students, a system that uses good authentication to show real person present should be designed.

2. ### **Problem Statements** {#problem-statements}

The current system, which is extensively used, is inefficient and time-consuming. It is tough to run an educational institute and conduct everyday activities in this circumstance. To deal with this problem, the manual attendance system takes a long time. The proposed method will make it more efficient and accurate.

Many educational institutes have been hit by the pandemic in recent years, and even after reopening, they have had a lot of issues in monitoring pupils, resulting in the neglect of SOPs.

It is a difficult effort to keep every student informed about current activities, as well as any delays or cancellations of courses; nevertheless, our proposed system includes an application that allows you to send out any information with a single touch.

3. ### **Aims and Objectives** {#aims-and-objectives}

The objectives of the project are shown as following:

1) To provide a cross platform application with user friendly features.  
2) To improve the efficiency for marking attendance and eliminate identity theft.  
3) To save paperwork and improve accuracy while also being environmentally sustainable.  
4) To provide real-time monitoring functionality in order to regulate SOP’s for COVID-19.

   4. ### **Scope of Project** {#scope-of-project}

Both rich and developing countries rely heavily on education for their development. This approach can be used in a variety of educational settings. The primary locations where this smart system can be applied are schools, colleges, offices and other institutions.  
This system is advantageous to both students and instructors, as it simplifies many issues that students and teachers face.  
The institute will be able to develop a more efficient strategy to address the current COVID problem by monitoring people's timeliness in real time and following the SOP's restrictions.

2. #  {#heading-1}

   1. ## **LITERATURE REVIEW** {#literature-review}

1.  **Literature Survey** 

Several research projects were conducted in the development of Attendance Management Systems. An end-to-end IoT solution for efficient management of educational institutions has been proposed as a prototype. \[2\]. The majority of the gadgets presented are either transportable or have hardware features like RFID and fingerprint sensors. \[3\]. Nonetheless, the goal at schools and colleges is to digitise the attendance management system. The proposed approach is to develop an IoT-based system with an application to monitor and control the environment in an institution. Maintaining an accountability on the activities of any individual entering and exiting the institute using a digitalized system would be considerably more efficient for the institution's administration and will help in the long run to reduce costs in the future. The current state of educational technology focuses on information sharing, network administration, and operational activity automation in educational institutions. \[4\].

Many institutions have installed and are operating their institutions using the above-mentioned management system technologies, but many developing countries, such as Pakistan, lack the digital essence of such systems, and many institutions lack even a basic understanding of how to incorporate such systems into their operations, which is where our proposed solution comes in.

2. **Existing Systems**

Attendance is important. In most educational institutions, hardware integration is used for control. RFID sensors, as well as door sensors, have shown to be efficient and effective. \[5\]. For attendance management and web monitoring, biometric fingerprint authentication is also available. \[6\]. A system with RFID tags, RFID readers and network connection \[7\] was proposed by the authors.

The goal is to create a simple and compact system that has all of the necessary capabilities and is easy to use.

The suggested framework would make it easier to monitor, regulate, and evaluate attendance on a regular basis. The system would considerably improve the efficiency of the faculty's work.

3. #  {#heading-2}

   1. ## **DESIGN AND METHODOLOGY** {#design-and-methodology}

**3.1	 Design**

At the design stage, the requirements will be further broken down in order to understand the project requirements more specifically. Stakeholders can better interact with the design than the document. The design phase is important for verifying and verifying the performance of the proposed design to ensure that it meets the requirements outlined during the requirements consolidation phase. The main goal at this stage is to create a prototype of the previously defined requirements that will be used during the development phase.

2. ### **Overview** {#overview}

The project focuses on accessibility and the primary objective is to provide remote access to the administration to monitor the conduct of the student and track attendance and for a student to review his attendance, time table and courses. The proposed system can be deployed on an existing institute's system,

The scope of this project includes only the provision of the following proposed working framework with all integration and implementation in place. 

![][image3]**Figure 3\. 1: System Framework**

**3.3	Organizational Structure**

Following the Organizational Structure for which the System is being designed. The main Users are defined as:

* Student  
* Admin

  1. #### **Student** {#student}

The students can access their room attendance information from the mobile application, view internship opportunities and the Newsletter. Student will have a smart card with an embedded tag for attendance using RFID to mark their attendance and have his facial features listed in the recognition system’s database and will be recognized by the system as a known personal of the institute and be allowed entrance in the premises.

2. #### **Admin** {#admin}

The admin can access room attendance as well as the entrance attendance list of the institution, the admin will be able to check whether the individuals entering the institute are following the COVID-19 SOP’s, that either the individual(s) who have entered the premises is/are wearing face masks or not wearing one. The Admin will have access of a real-time view of the camera feed as well as the generated list of attending individuals

4. ### **Methodology** {#methodology}

The Methodology process model we implemented is chosen to be Agile. Agile is an iterative and incremental development process that is performed in a highly collaborative manner by self-organizing teams within a real control structure. It is extremely responsive in terms of delivering solutions to satisfy the changing needs of its constituents. Agile methodologies ensure a higher degree of customer satisfaction, a lower defect rate, improved usability, and a solution that is exceptionally flexible to changing requirements. \[10\]

Following Stages are involved in the Smart Education Institute:

![][image4]

**Figure 3\. 2  Methodology Diagram**

## 

1. #### **Information Gathering** {#information-gathering}

It is difficult to create a solution if you do not know the requirements. The first phase is the phase of data aggregation which addresses the need to develop a new system by analysing the problems in the existing system. Team members describe the scope and limitations of the proposed system. The goal for development at this stage is clear, but the steps required to achieve the goal may vary. It concerns the technical feasibility of the system associated with the risk.

2. #### **Design** {#design}

   At the design stage, the requirements will be further broken down in order to understand the project requirements more specifically. Stakeholders can better interact with the design than the document. The design phase is important for verifying and verifying the performance of the proposed design to ensure that it meets the requirements outlined during the requirements consolidation phase. The main goal at this stage is to create a prototype of the previously defined requirements that will be used during the development phase.

 


   3. #### **Development** {#development}

   The development phase begins when the design phase is completed. Developers begin by writing source code in accordance with previously specified specifications. The role of front-end developers is to create the application's user interface as well as the logic for its server interactions, whereas the role of backend developers is to manage the database and create APIs for data handling. \[11\]

      4. #### **Testing** {#testing}

   The testing phase involves the process of debugging and debugging the software application and checking whether the application is functioning properly as per the requirements of the user. At this stage the software tester checks for code errors that may be unchecked during the development phase. Documentation to pass on to developers to fix them after these deficiencies. It also checks, to ensure that the software is free from any kind of errors and flaws, the actual result matches the expected result. The testing process is repeated until all critical issues have been resolved and the software workflow has stabilized. \[11\]

   

   

   

      5. #### **Reviews** {#reviews}

   Once the software has been tested and it meets all the requirements specified in the requirements specification document, then the software goes to the next stage, i.e. reviews. At this stage, we will review the work done by our FYP supervisor and what to do next. If the developed facility requires further development, we will repeat and move on to Phase 2, i.e., Towards the design phase.

 


      6. #### **Maintenance** {#maintenance}

   In this phase, systems are up and running, and enhancements and/or adjustments are being developed and tested in order to improve system efficiency. During the maintenance phase, we will add new features and modules to the application in order to issue fresh upgrades, the system's performance is monitored on a regular basis in order to improve its efficiency, effectiveness, and security. When changes are found, the system may re-enter the design phase.

      7. ###  **Data gathering and Initial requirements** {#data-gathering-and-initial-requirements}

6. **RFID Smart Card Attendance using NodeMCU**

# 

RFID stands for "Radio Frequency Identification." RFID modules employ electromagnetic fields to transport data between the card and the reader. RFID tags are affixed to various things such as keychains, cards, and so on, and the reader scans the tags whenever the object is placed in front of the RFID reader. The advantage of RFID is that it may be identified without having to be in a straight line. Unlike a barcode, RFID has no such restriction. 

When the user with the correct RFID card swipes his or her RFID tag, the RFID NodeMCU Module records his or her attendance. To send the card UID to the database, we used a NodeMCU ESP8266 development board with an MF-RC522 module.

![][image11]  
**Figure 3.9 RFID Attendance System using NodeMCU**

7.      **Facial Recognition & Face Mask Detection**

Face recognition is one of the most popular biometrics methods as opposed to any other methods, recognition offers a contactless solution that meets the needs of today's scenarios in comparison to Iris recognition, fingerprint analysis, or palm print analysis.  
Facial recognition system compares a human face from a digital image or a video frame to a database of faces by locating and quantifying facial features from the image. It's often used by identity verification services to verify users.

For face recognition, we have used an implementation of a unique Haar-cascade classifier which is paired with LBP and eigenfaces. Due to the requirement for pandemic COVID-19 prevention, the facemask detection is included in the attendance system, which varies from the already existing face recognition system.

The system begins with an image obtained from the entry video camera. Two cameras were employed, one for entry records and the other for exit records, one at the entrance door and the other at the exit door. Attendees' faces were photographed and sent into the system for face detection. The system will undertake mask detection once the face has been spotted. The device will perform face recognition if the person is not wearing a mask. Otherwise, the system will display the word 'Using Mask' on the screen, reminding the user to remove his or her mask. The face recognition module compares the image of the captured face to the photographs in the face database. Finally, the database updates with the attendance information of recognized attendees as well as the time captured during detection. At the exit door, the identical process is performed, with two distinct times being recorded for the final computation of time spent for each attendance.   
![][image12]  
**Figure 3.10. Face Recognition and Mask Detection Framework**

1. **Face and Mask Detection**

We used the work of \[12\] for the face detection problem. First, a Haar-like feature representation was used to represent the photographs. Second, AdaBoost was employed to improve classification accuracy. We used the custom Haar-cascade \[13\] for mask detection. Positive and negative photographs were used to train the cascade function. Positive photographs were those in which a facemask is visible. Negative photographs of faces without facemasks. Pre-processing that included contrast correction, intensity normalization, and size normalizing was performed on each of the photographs where the face was successfully recognized. After that, the pre-processed photographs were delivered to the facial recognition module.

2. **Face Recognition**

Face recognition was done using Eigenfaces and the local binary pattern histogram (LBPH). These algorithms were chosen because their implementation takes less time. Furthermore, both have been demonstrated to be possible in a real-time context and to generate good recognition results. \[14-16\].

3. **Face recognition using Eigenfaces**

Eigenfaces is a holistic or subspace-based method that employed PCA to identify a set of features that defined variance among images. Due to its advantages in extracting relevant facial information and efficient face picture representation, it has been employed for face detection and recognition \[17\]. The eigenfaces were calculated for each image in the training set, and only the images with the highest eigenvalues were chosen. After that, the weights for each of the chosen images were calculated and projected to the eigenspace. Similar to the stages before, the eigenvectors must be determined to recognize an unfamiliar face.

4. **Face Recognition using LBPH**

Due to its computational simplicity in real-time and resistance to monotonic greyscale changes such as light, LBP has been applied in a wide range of implementations \[18\]. LBP is a local based appearance method that uses texture information taken from an image's frontal perspective as features. Its thresholds the neighbour of each surrounding pixel to identify the pixels in a picture.

2. ###  **Face Recognition** {#face-recognition}

   1. **The Implementation of the Proposed System**

For implementation, the unique Haar cascade classifier and the best-performing face recognition algorithm, the LBPH are employed. Three key modules make up the system's implementation. Data face recording, mask detection and facial recognition, and attendance output creation are among the modules.

2. **Data Face Recording**

   

The data face recording module collected photos of participants and stored them in a database. The system first scans members' faces and captures them using the name or ID provided. Under the correspondence folder, only a unique name or ID is preserved to the database. Before being stored in the database, the facial image was scaled, converted to greyscale, and normalized. A sample of photos taken, pre-processed, and stored in the database is shown in Figure 4.1.

![][image27] ![][image28] ![][image29]

**Figure 4.1 (a) Original captured image, (b) Image was detected and resized., (c) Image in greyscale and stored in the database**

3. **Mask Detection and Face Recognition**

Two phases are involved in the mask detection and face recognition module. The subject's face is detected first, and then the mask is detected. The system displays the warning 'using mask' if the individual is wearing a facemask. If no facemask is identified, the LBPH is then used to perform the recognition procedure. The name of the subject is printed on the screen for each recognized face, and the subject's record is saved in the database. The system keeps track of the subject's name, as well as the day and time of recognition, i.e., attendance in and exit. Figure 4.2 depicts examples of mask detection and subject face recognition.

![][image30]![][image31]

**Figure 4.2 (a) Due to mask occlusion, there is an unknown face detection with a notice warning., (b) After removing the mask, the recognition is correct.**

4. **Attendance Output Generation**

The attendance report generation is the final module of the implementation. The report provides information such as arrival and exit times, as well as total time spent in a class or event. Figure 4.3 shows a screenshot of the generated attendance report.

![][image32]

**Figure 4.3 Attendance Report Generation**

The code uses OpenCv to open camera to collect images for facial recognition, then it asks the user to save face image and converts it into grey scale and prompts a save as dialog box which allows the user to save the grey scale facial image to the location where the image set is needs to be saved and asks the user to input the name/id of whom the images where collected, the “Collect Images” needs 10 images to be saved for the model to be trained (User must not be wearing a mask while taking these images).

5. #  {#heading-4}

   1. ## **RESULTS AND DISCUSSION** {#results-and-discussion}

In this chapter, we'll talk about product testing to see if the application is successful, efficient, and dependable. In order to test an application, it must go through a series of steps. We ensure that the application or product is working properly and effectively after passing these phases, and that it is ready to send to the customer. If a problem arises during testing, it is the responsibility of the developers to resolve the issue before releasing the product.

2. ### **TESTING** {#testing-1}

Testing is a way of locating flaws in software applications and determining whether or not the application's functions are performing as expected by the user. \[27\] It also verifies that the actual result matches the predicted result, ensuring that the programme is free of mistakes and faults. Software testing is the process of validating and verifying an application or piece of software. \[28\]  
Testing also aids in the discovery of software problems that the developer may have missed. 

Testing is carried out in order to achieve the following goals:

* To point out any flaws or faults that may have occurred during the development process.  
* To meet the needs of customers.  
* To ensure that the application/product is of high quality.  
* To eliminate flaws.

  3. ### **TESTING METHODS** {#testing-methods}

The types of testing are as follows:

1. White box Testing  
2. Black box Testing

## 

   1. #### **White Box Testing** {#white-box-testing}

White box testing is a type of code-based testing that examines the system's internal functions. All code statements, paths, and circumstances are addressed in white box testing. Internal code implementation and structure are known by the tester in White box testing. Low-level testing is another name for this method of testing. \[29\] 

![][image80]  
**Figure 5\. 1 White box Testing**

2. #### **Black Box Testing** {#black-box-testing}

External testing or user end perspective is used in black box testing. The goal of this testing methodology was to see if the predicted result was obtained or not. The focus of black box testing is on an application's behaviour. \[29\] The tester is unaware of the internal code in this methodology. High level testing is another name for black box testing.

![][image81]  
**Figure 5\. 2 Black box Testing**

To test our application, we employed both black box and white box testing approaches.

Some of the black box testing approaches utilised in the project are listed below.

* Usability testing  
* Unit testing  
* Integration testing  
* System testing  
* User interface testing.

  4. ### **TEST CASES** {#test-cases}

5. ###  **OUTCOME** {#outcome}

The outcome of this project:

* A User-Friendly Mobile Application to edit/view an Institute’s Newsletter, Internship Opportunities and Attendance.  
* Attendance system comprising of Facial Recognition along with the capability to detect masks in accordance for following COVID-19 SOP’s.  
* A room attendance system comprising of NodeMCU using RFID tagging to mark attendance.

Final deliverable of the project:

* An android application  
* Facial Recognition system with Mask Detection  
* NodeMCU Attendance system using RFID Tags

Benefit of the project:

* More Security for Institutions  
* Monitoring of Conduct of SOP’s  
* Automated Attendance  
* Mobile Application to edit/view an Institute’s Newsletter, Internship Opportunities and Attendance.

6. #  {#heading-5}

   1. ## **CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATIONS** {#conclusion-and-recommendations}

      2. ###  **CONCLUSION** {#conclusion}

For the system to conform with the current pandemic condition, a framework of mask detection incorporated in facial recognition was developed. Image input, face detection, mask detection, face recognition, and attendance recording are all part of the framework. For mask and face detection, the Haar cascade was used. The eigenfaces and LBPH face recognition techniques were employed. The LBPH outperformed the Eigenfaces in the face recognition tests. The usefulness of the strategy to employ face recognition to register attendance has been demonstrated in an initial experiment and deployment.

A NodeMCU module incorporated with RFID was used for attendance and both the results of the attendance from Facial Recognition and Node Module were introduced into a single MongoDB database which was connected to the developed mobile application called ‘SEI’ to view the attendance along with incorporating the Newsletter and Internship opportunities provided by the Institute with the Student being able to only view and Admin to have create/update/delete privileges.

3. ###  **FUTURE WORK** {#future-work}

An examination of a technique capable of performing partial face occlusion identification utilising a partial face image can be done. Face identification without the requirement for the subjects to remove their facemask or masked face recognition, which is required in some countries because to the COVID-19 pandemic, would be possible.

The application ‘SEI’ can be further enhanced to have more functionality by introducing online Quiz systems, Multiple Institute Management and incorporating different language support i.e German, Chinese, Russian, Japanese, Indonesian for ease of accessibility for foreign exchange students.
